interest: This document is particularly valuable to diplomatic and military historians of East Asia as a consolidated chronological register of Japanese naval movements, force projection, and gunboat diplomacy along the China coast and the Yangtze River between 1930 and 1934. It highlights how the U.S. State Department systematically tracked Japanese naval escalation during the Manchurian Crisis and the 1932 Shanghai Incident, cross-referencing field reports to broader political files (793.94). The document captures key localized flashpoints—including marine landings at Tsingtao, gunboat intimidation of the Chinese National Government at Nanking, skirmishes at Pootung/Nantao, conflicts of authority between Japanese consular and naval officers, and maritime smuggling operations from Dairen into Shantung.
overview: This file comprises the U.S. Department of State's official List of Papers (Form DS-46) for decimal file 894.3393, which served as an index and cross-reference register for diplomatic and consular reports regarding visits and activities of Japanese naval vessels and aircraft in Chinese ports from April 1930 to October 1934. Because substantive reports on Japanese military and naval operations in China were categorized under political relations (chiefly decimal file 793.94) or China internal affairs (893.00), this file consists of cross-reference entries noting thirty-eight separate communications. The entries document the movements, port visits, and deployments of Japanese destroyers, cruisers (including the Izumo, Yakumo, and Kuma), aircraft carriers, and landing parties across major treaty ports—notably Shanghai, Nanking, Tsingtao, Chefoo, Hankow, and Tientsin—during the heightened tensions of the Manchurian Crisis and the January 28 Shanghai Incident of 1932, as well as Japanese junk smuggling and fishing operations off Shantung.

subfiles.about: A Department of State list of papers recording cross-reference entries for reports and correspondence concerning visits, deployments, and movements of Japanese naval vessels to Chinese ports from 1930 to 1934.
subfiles.summary: This two-page List of Papers (Form DS-46) catalogs thirty-eight cross-referenced communications in State Department file 894.3393 concerning the visits, stationing, and activities of Japanese naval vessels and aircraft in Chinese ports between April 1930 and October 1934. The entries refer researchers to substantive documentation filed primarily under 793.94 (Sino-Japanese political relations) and 893.00 (China internal affairs), transmitted by American diplomatic and consular officials in Tokyo, Peiping, Shanghai, Nanking, Tsingtao, Chefoo, Tientsin, and Hankow. Key historical events referenced include the deployment of cruisers, destroyers, and an aircraft carrier during the 1932 Shanghai Incident; the anchorage of Japanese warships off Nanking to intimidate the Chinese National Government; landing of marines and squadron visits at Tsingtao; and Japanese junk smuggling operations from Dairen into Shantung.
